notes: OpenAPI /v2/networks/{network}/metrics/{metric}: Gets staking metrics for a given subnet. NetworkMetric enum: delegatorCount, delegatorWeight, validatorCount, validatorWeight.

OpenAPI /v2/chains/{chainId}/metrics/{metric}: EVM chain metrics are available for all Avalanche L1s on Mainnet and Fuji. All metrics are updated several times every hour. Each metric data point has a value and timestamp (Unix timestamp in seconds). All metric values include data within the duration of the associated timestamp plus the requested timeInterval. All timestamps are fixed to the hour.
OpenAPI MetricsValue.value: Aggregated value for the current metrics. MetricsValue.timestamp: Unix Epoch timestamp for which metrics are aggregated; for a day interval this is the start of the day.

Chain 43114 is the C-Chain. The API serves no P-Chain chain metrics (HTTP 404 for the Primary Network subnet ID), so P-Chain fees and burn come from the Snowflake P_TRANSACTIONS columns FEE and BURNED_AVAX instead.
Both series begin 2021-01-01; earlier dates are absent from the API although the Primary Network has staking history from 2020-09-10.

Reconciliation on 2026-09-19 against the end-of-day active set rebuilt from the Snowflake validator and delegator datasets: validator counts differ by a median 1.1 percent in 2021 to 2023, 2.1 percent in 2024, 2.8 percent in 2025, and 3.4 percent in 2026; delegator counts by 1.5 to 2.4 percent in 2021 to 2022 and 5.5 to 8 percent from 2023. Sampled days in 2022 and 2024 match exactly at end of day, so the residual reflects the API's undocumented aggregation instant plus an undercount from 2025 that also skips nine days between 2025-10-12 and 2025-12-01.

notes: OpenAPI GET /v1/avax/supply: Get AVAX supply information that includes total supply, circulating supply, total p burned, total c burned, total x burned, total staked, total locked, total rewards, and last updated. The operation takes no parameters.

Blocker recorded 2026-09-19: the Data API exposes no historical supply, circulating supply, staked supply, or cumulative burn series; the supply endpoint returns one current state with lastUpdated. A history can only be assembled by repeated captures or from the Snowflake block supply counter.
Observed 2026-09-19: totalSupply equals genesisUnlock plus totalRewards minus the three burn totals to within one AVAX, so the API's totals are internally consistent.

C-Chain atomic transaction listing pages backward from latest; startTimestamp and endTimestamp require an address filter, so a complete all-address dated capture walks pages until it crosses the requested start.

Validators endpoint, measured 2026-09-22: 100 rows per page is the maximum, about four seconds a page, no rate-limit headers, and Cloudflare rejects Python's default user agent. Without a subnetId filter the endpoint also returns subnet validators, which have no delegation fee. Active Primary Network validations carry uptimePerformance as observed by Ava Labs' node; completed validations carry rewards and reward addresses but no uptime, so historical uptime percentages are not recoverable from this API.

C-Chain block record, measured 2026-09-23: GET /v1/chains/43114/blocks/{height} returns the block's feesSpent, an integer number of wei equal to the sum of gas used times effective gas price over its receipts; the block listing takes no height range, so gap blocks are read one request each

Rate limit, measured 2026-09-23: keyless, the API answered HTTP 429 after about 130 requests at three a second and again after about 1,000 requests at one a second, and kept refusing for more than ten minutes; a key would raise the limit and is never stored in the repository
With a key, measured 2026-09-23: the response carries ratelimit-policy 8000;w=60, cost units per minute, and a block request costs about ten, so about 750 block requests a minute

Three P-Chain ImportTx of 2022-01-15 and 2022-01-16 record a negative BURNED_AVAX; a negative record is read as no record, and the UTXO method gives each the 0.001 AVAX pre-Etna import fee

AdvanceTimeTx and RewardValidatorTx carry no burn; genesis transactions (2020-09-10, block height -1) carry none either, confirmed on all 77 P and 1 X genesis hashes against the Data API on 2026-09-21
A null burn outside those cases is inputs minus non-reward outputs over the AVAX UTXOs the share holds for the hash; the method reproduced BURNED_AVAX on 30 P and 60 X control transactions

For IncreaseL1ValidatorBalanceTx, RegisterL1ValidatorTx, and ConvertSubnetToL1Tx, BURNED_AVAX includes the L1 validator balance deposited (L1_VALIDATOR_PAYG_BALANCE per validator row); the deposit is subtracted from the burn and reported apart, matching the Data API's amountBurned and amountL1ValidatorBalanceBurned on ten sampled transactions

L1 validator fees accrue continuously from those balances: L1_VALIDATOR_ACCRUED_FEES is a per-validator cumulative counter and L1_VALIDATOR_ACTIVE_COUNT the validators paying it, so the fee burned between two P transactions is the previous count times the counter's increase; summed to 2026-09-19 11:00 UTC this gives 17,951.43 AVAX against the Data API's 17,951.41

The Data API's totalPBurned equals these transaction burns plus the L1 validator fees; its totalXBurned equals the recorded X burns and omits the 612 null-burn X transactions of 2025-09-13 to 2025-09-15 that the UTXO method settles at 0.679 AVAX

sources.name: Avalanche Builder Hub validator explorer
sources.authority: Ava Labs' Builder Hub, which proxies a validator-metrics service fed by the nodes Ava Labs runs. Its uptime is the hourly median across those observers: one observer set, beside the public P-Chain RPC node and the Data API, and not the protocol's own stake-weighted vote at period end.
sources.authentication: none
sources.reuse_status: Public access observed; no terms published for these routes. Redistribution terms unassessed.
notes: Measured 2026-09-23 and 2026-09-24: the list route returns a JSON array of about 611 current Primary Network validators; the detail route returns, per node, hourly uptime buckets for a rolling window of 332 hours, daily bench totals, hourly block proposals and misses, and a 14-day summary of the underlying observations (116,017 for one node). A validator that has ended still answers.

Changed between the captures of 2026-09-27 00:45 UTC and 2026-09-29 19:17 UTC: the window is about 175 hours, each detail carries observed_at, the hours both captures hold were restated (74% of settled node-hours differ, by 0.016 percentage points on average and 11.4 at most, where consecutive captures had agreed exactly), and 10 of 11 validators that had ended answer HTTP 500.
The route caches each answer for five minutes and, when its upstream fails, answers from cache with the response header X-Data-Source: error-fallback-cache, which the capture records per node.
The routes proxy a service at a bare address (52.203.183.9.sslip.io); the capture calls the published Builder Hub routes, not the address.
The slots series (slot, count) is kept in the raw lines and not built into a table; its meaning is undocumented.

sources.name: Derived datasets
sources.authority: No external authority. A derived dataset is a deterministic transformation of built runs of other datasets in this catalog, and inherits their authority and limits. Its receipt records the exact input runs and their hashes.
sources.authentication: none; built locally from data/runs
sources.reuse_status: Follows the reuse status of its inputs.
notes: Built with `avalanche data derive`, which selects the newest built run of each input unless a run is pinned, and writes a capture receipt naming the input runs beside the Parquet build.
The staking-period log adds the network upgrade regime at acceptance and the reward the protocol kernel computes for each row, so the recorded potential reward can be checked row by row.

The node table folds the staking-period log, the reward addresses on validator transactions, and the delegator addresses into one row per validator node. Its clocks are clipped at the validator capture time, so a run is reproducible from its inputs alone.

The monetary daily ledger replays supply from genesis: rewards paid out minus burns on every chain, in wei, with a coverage state per component and per day, and takes every current run of the multi-run inputs so repairs captured later fill earlier gaps without a rebuild of the sources.

The hourly validator uptime table merges every Builder Hub capture into one row per node per hour, keeping the newest capture's value, the number of captures that held the hour, and whether any two disagreed. Daily captures overlap by about six days since the source shortened its window to about 175 hours, so the table grows without gaps while captures continue. Hours the source restated keep the newest value and are marked revised.

sources.name: Avalanche Foundation Snowflake account: Allium's Avalanche database and the Foundation's Gross Chain Product database
sources.authority: The Avalanche Foundation's Snowflake account, read-only, under the Foundation's agreement, through a named connection. It holds the database AVALANCHE, Allium's indexed C-Chain data with its hourly token price service and its prices derived from decentralised exchange trades, and the database AF, the Foundation's Gross Chain Product pipeline. Authoritative for the rows it exposes as Allium and the Foundation compute them, not for the price of AVAX on any one venue or for the full C-Chain fee burn. Each query names its database and schema in full; the database and schema fields here are those of the first dataset.

fields.name: realized_reward_avax

fields.unit: nAVAX; positive is delegation fee income to a validator, negative is fee paid by a delegator
fields.derivation: realized_reward_navax minus potential_reward_navax. Sign and meaning depend on the row: a rewarded delegation to a validator added at or after Cortina reads minus (potential reward times the validator's fee rate), the fee withheld and paid to the validator at its own period end; a rewarded delegation to a validator added before Cortina reads zero, because its reward UTXOs included the validator's share; a rewarded validator period reads plus the delegatee rewards it accrued since Cortina; any period that realised zero reads minus its potential reward. Fee income and fee paid are therefore derived from rate times potential, never read from this field (node table plan NC2, glossary G15). The derived check reconciles the post-Cortina delegations.

datasets.name: AVAX monetary daily ledger
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
Value Accrual as Equilibrium: How We Think About AVAX Tokenomics
From Gross Chain Product to Gross Chain Income: Where the Value Goes
datasets.description: One row per UTC date with recognised staking reward issuance, AVAX burned on the P-, X-, and C-Chains, realised total supply replayed from genesis and stake active at the day's last second. Ordinary rewards retain net payout timing. Auto-renewed cycles recognise current self rewards and pending delegatee fees once at a verified reward event, excluding release of previously recognised restake. Cycle weights determine active stake. Amounts are integer wei, with explicit coverage. Supply stops at the first incomplete day.

fields.name: date_utc
fields.derivation: one row per calendar day from the 2020-09-10 genesis to the last complete day of the P and X burn run

fields.name: issued_rewards_wei
fields.derivation: ordinary reward transaction net outputs, excluding auto-renewed parent payouts, plus current cycle self rewards and pending delegatee fees at the verified cycle proposal and matching commit or abort; prior restaked accrual released on exit is not new issuance; nAVAX times 10^9

fields.name: burned_p_wei
fields.derivation: burned_p_transactions_wei plus burned_p_l1_validator_fees_wei: the P-Chain burn as the Data API's totalPBurned defines it

fields.name: burned_p_transactions_wei
fields.derivation: AVAX destroyed by P-Chain transactions accepted that day, from snowflake.primary-burn-daily, plus the burns of that day's unresolved transactions settled by p-chain-rpc.transactions, times 10^9

fields.name: burned_p_l1_validator_fees_wei
fields.derivation: L1 validator fees burned from validator balances that day, from snowflake.primary-burn-daily, times 10^9

fields.name: burned_x_wei
fields.derivation: AVAX destroyed by X-Chain transactions accepted that day, from snowflake.primary-burn-daily, times 10^9

fields.name: burned_c_evm_wei
fields.derivation: C-Chain EVM fees of the day's blocks: the share's complete blocks from snowflake.c-chain-evm-burn-daily plus burned_c_evm_gap_wei

fields.name: burned_c_evm_gap_wei
fields.derivation: fees of the day's gap blocks read from the Data API block record (data-api.c-chain-block-fees), a public node's receipts (c-chain-rpc.block-receipt-fees), or the archived node receipts (c-chain-rpc.receipt-gap-repairs), dated by the block's own timestamp; where two sources hold a block they must agree to the wei

fields.name: burned_c_atomic_wei
fields.derivation: AVAX unlocked minus created by the day's C-Chain imports and exports, from data-api.c-chain-atomic-burn, with each import the API leaves unsettled taken from c-chain-rpc.atomic-transactions, times 10^9

fields.name: burned_wei
fields.derivation: burned_p_wei + burned_x_wei + burned_c_evm_wei + burned_c_atomic_wei

fields.name: total_supply_open_wei
fields.derivation: the previous day's total_supply_close_wei; 360,000,000 AVAX on the genesis day

fields.name: total_supply_close_wei
fields.derivation: total_supply_open_wei + issued_rewards_wei - burned_wei, written only while every day from genesis through this one is complete, null after the first incomplete day

fields.name: active_validator_stake_wei
fields.derivation: ordinary validator stake on [start_time, end_time), plus each auto-renewed cycle weight on its verified half-open interval, evaluated at 23:59:59 UTC; nAVAX times 10^9

fields.name: active_delegated_stake_wei
fields.derivation: stake of delegator periods active at the same instant, times 10^9

fields.name: active_validators
fields.derivation: validator periods active at the instant

fields.name: active_delegations
fields.derivation: delegator periods active at the instant

fields.name: rewards_coverage
fields.derivation: complete only inside the ordinary reward source window and before its capture day, with required cycle history and reward events verified through the admitted horizon; missing outside the window; unresolved past cycle events refuse the build

fields.name: p_coverage
fields.derivation: 'complete' when the day has no unresolved P transaction, 'repaired' when every unresolved one is settled by a node record, 'incomplete' otherwise, 'missing' outside the burn run

fields.name: x_coverage
fields.derivation: as p_coverage, for the X-Chain

fields.name: c_evm_coverage
fields.derivation: 'complete' when the day lies inside a C EVM run and has no absent or short block, 'repaired' when every gap block the gaps run lists for the day has a fee record, 'incomplete' otherwise, 'missing' outside every run; days before the first C block are complete at zero

fields.name: c_atomic_coverage

fields.name: stake_coverage
fields.derivation: 'complete' for days before the staking-period inputs were captured, else 'missing'

fields.name: complete
fields.derivation: every coverage is complete or repaired

datasets.name: Validation cycles started after Helicon
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per Primary Network validation cycle that started at or after Helicon's activation on 2026-09-22 15:00 UTC, which lowered the minimum validator duration from 14 days to 48 hours and added auto-renewal. A cycle is a distinct transaction hash and start time, because an auto-renewed validation keeps its hash while its start and end move forward. Built from every snapshot run of the validator set, so a renewal seen between two snapshots is kept, and from the staking-period log for each node's history before Helicon. Each cycle carries its duration and bin, whether its node validated before Helicon, and the change from the node's previous validator period. The build summary compares the bins with the validator periods started in the 30 days before activation. Cycles are known only from the snapshots: one that starts and ends between two snapshots is not seen.

fields.name: node_id
fields.derivation: the validator node, a node and not an operator (glossary G1)

fields.name: transaction_hash
fields.derivation: the validator staking transaction, shared by every cycle of an auto-renewed validation

fields.name: cycle_start
fields.derivation: start_time of the cycle in the snapshots, at or after 2026-09-22 15:00 UTC

fields.name: cycle_end
fields.derivation: end_time of the cycle in the first snapshot showing it

fields.name: duration_days
fields.derivation: cycle_end minus cycle_start in seconds over 86,400 (glossary G5)

fields.name: stake_avax
fields.derivation: own stake in the first snapshot showing the cycle. An auto-renewed validation can restake its reward, so it may grow from one cycle to the next

fields.name: delegation_fee_rate
fields.derivation: delegation fee rate in the first snapshot showing the cycle (glossary G12)

fields.name: first_seen_at
fields.derivation: observed_at of the first snapshot showing the cycle

fields.name: cycle_number
fields.derivation: 1 for the first observed cycle of the transaction, 2 and up for each auto-renewal, in start order

fields.name: auto_renewed
fields.derivation: the transaction has more than one observed cycle. A transaction still in its first cycle reads false until it renews

fields.name: node_status
fields.derivation: returning when the node has a validator period starting before activation in the staking-period log or in an earlier snapshot, else new

fields.name: previous_duration_days
fields.derivation: duration of the node's latest validator period that started before this cycle, from the staking-period log or the snapshots. For a renewal it is the previous cycle. Null when the node has no earlier period

fields.name: duration_change_days
fields.derivation: duration_days minus previous_duration_days, null when there is no previous period

datasets.name: Daily market vector before the held-back cut: AVAX return and realised variance, Bitcoin return, log gas burn
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per UTC day from 2021-02-02 to 2025-11-18, the day before the held-back cut of 2025-11-19: the AVAX close at 24:00 UTC and its log return, the realised variance as the sum of squared hourly log returns within the day (Corsi 2009, https://doi.org/10.1093/jjfinec/nbp001) with the number of hourly returns used, the Bitcoin close and log return at the same instant from Coin Metrics, and the natural log of the day's C-Chain gas burn. The hourly AVAX price is Allium's, read through the Avalanche Foundation's read-only Snowflake account under the Foundation's agreement: from 2022-06-01 01:00 UTC its price service's native AVAX price, with its WAVAX price where the native row is missing, and before that its WAVAX price from decentralised exchange trades, which starts on 2021-02-02 15:00 UTC. Days before 2021-02-02 have no hourly AVAX price and no row. The column price_source records which table each close came from. The exchange price is smoother than the service's, so the change of table lowers the realised variance before 2022-06-01; dex_realised_variance gives the exchange table's figure on every day it covers. The gas burn is the Foundation economy's count, about 13% below Allium's whole-chain fee total. No row is dated on or after the cut and nothing observed after 2025-11-19 00:00 UTC is read; the check rebuilds the table from its inputs cut at that instant and requires the same rows. The check also compares each close with DefiLlama's daily price at the same midnight, a reference no field reads. Lending-rate and outside-yield columns are planned to follow these fields and are not built yet.

datasets.name: Daily revenue streams of sAVAX, the stablecoin issuers and the tokenised funds
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per protocol, day, stream, token and chain of the Foundation's protocol stream metrics, read from its Snowflake account under the Foundation's agreement: BENQI's liquid staking token sAVAX, with its staking yield and its payout to holders, and the issuer yield of stablecoin issuers and the holder yield of tokenised bill and yield funds, each in tokens, USD and AVAX. datasets.name: Aave v3 WAVAX supply rate by day, DefiLlama's series with its gaps filled from Allium
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per UTC day of DefiLlama's Aave v3 WAVAX supply rate, the series aave-wavax of derived.opportunity-costs-daily from 2022-08-08, with its two gaps filled: 2024-01-04 to 2024-01-10 and 2024-10-09 to 2025-03-09, 159 days, each filled with the mean of supply_apy over the day's Allium rate updates of protocol aave_v3 and token WAVAX, read from the Avalanche Foundation's Snowflake account, read-only, under the Foundation's agreement, through a named connection. Every DefiLlama value is kept and the field source names each row's table, so the series changes only where it was empty. Both are annual percentage yields in percent of the supplied amount a year. Allium's daily mean, median and update count stand beside every row it covers. The check rebuilds the table, requires every DefiLlama value kept and every fill day filled, and requires Allium's mean within 0.10 points of DefiLlama's on average, with a correlation of at least 0.95, on the 60 days both cover in 1 September to 8 October 2024 and 10 to 31 March 2025. The capture names the lending run's Snowflake query ID and query-text hash.

datasets.name: Three outside yields by decision day before the held-back cut: AVAX lending composite, sAVAX yield, hedged bill rate
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per decision day from 2021-02-02 to 2025-11-18, the day before the held-back cut of 2025-11-19, with three outside yields in percent a year, each as the raw value of the day before the decision and the median of the 7 days before it, kept when at least 4 have a value. The AVAX lending composite is the supply rate of the Avalanche lending markets for AVAX and WAVAX that record one, weighted by each market's supplied AVAX at its last update of the day, from Allium's lending rate updates; a day with no rated update takes the filled Aave v3 WAVAX rate. Compound v2 forks, BENQI among them, record no supply rate in Allium's table and are left out, and their supplied AVAX is reported beside the composite. The liquid staking yield is the 30-day growth of the sAVAX exchange rate, sAVAX over AVAX in Allium's hourly prices at 24:00 UTC, compounded to a year. The hedged bill rate is the 3-month bill rate, from the Foundation's benchmark table on its FRED and carried-forward days and from FRED's last published value otherwise, less Binance's AVAX perpetual funding rate annualised. The Allium and Foundation inputs are read from the Avalanche Foundation's Snowflake account, read-only, under the Foundation's agreement, through a named connection. Nothing observed after 2025-11-19 00:00 UTC is read; the check rebuilds the table from its inputs cut at that instant and requires the same rows.

fields.name: date_utc
fields.unit: UTC ISO date of the decision
fields.derivation: every calendar day from 2021-02-02 to 2025-11-18; every other field reads only days before it

fields.name: lending_pct
fields.unit: percent of the supplied amount a year
fields.derivation: the lending composite of the day before

fields.name: lending_source
fields.derivation: allium-composite when a rated AVAX or WAVAX market updated that day, otherwise the filled Aave v3 WAVAX rate

fields.name: lending_markets
fields.derivation: rated markets in the composite of the day before; 0 when the Aave rate stands in

fields.name: lending_supplied_avax
fields.derivation: the composite's total weight: supplied_amount at each rated market's last update of the day before

fields.name: lending_unrated_supplied_avax
fields.derivation: supplied_amount of AVAX and WAVAX markets without a supply rate that updated the day before, left out of the composite

fields.name: lending_median_7d_pct
fields.derivation: median of the composite over the 7 days before the decision; null with fewer than 4

fields.name: lending_days_7d
fields.derivation: days in that median

fields.name: savax_exchange_rate
fields.derivation: Allium's sAVAX price over its native AVAX price, WAVAX where native is missing, both stamped at 24:00 UTC of the day before

fields.name: savax_growth_30d_pct
fields.derivation: ((rate / rate 30 days earlier) ** (365 / 30) - 1) * 100 for the day before

fields.name: savax_median_7d_pct
fields.derivation: median of the growth over the 7 days before the decision; null with fewer than 4

fields.name: savax_days_7d
fields.derivation: days in that median

fields.name: bill_pct
fields.derivation: DTB3 of the day before: the benchmark table's rate times 100 on its FRED DTB3 and carried-forward days, otherwise FRED's last published value on or before it

fields.name: bill_source
fields.derivation: the table bill_pct comes from

fields.name: funding_pct
fields.unit: percent of position value a year
fields.derivation: Binance AVAXUSDT mean funding rate per 8-hour event on the day before times 3 times 365 times 100

fields.name: funding_events
fields.derivation: events on the day before, 3 on a complete day

fields.name: hedged_bill_pct
fields.derivation: bill_pct less funding_pct

fields.name: hedged_median_7d_pct
fields.derivation: median of the hedged bill rate over the 7 days before the decision; null with fewer than 4

fields.name: hedged_days_7d
fields.derivation: days in that median

datasets.name: The liquid staking yield from sAVAX's contract rate, by decision day before the held-back cut
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per decision day from 2022-01-28 to 2025-11-18 with the 30-day liquid staking yield read from the AVAX one sAVAX redeems for in BENQI's contract, the yield a holder of sAVAX earns. It sits beside derived.outside-yields-daily, whose price-ratio yield is unchanged. A row is dated by the decision day d and reads the state at day d-1's last block. The yield is the rate's growth over 30 days compounded to a year, in percent, and the 7-day median is the median of the yields of days d-7 to d-1 that have a value, kept when at least 4 do. The market discount, Allium's hourly sAVAX over AVAX price at 24:00 UTC of day d-1 over the contract rate less 1, is a separate column and not a yield. No row is dated on or after 2025-11-19 and every state read is at a block before 2025-11-19 00:00 UTC. The check requires that, one row per decision day, and the same rows from a rebuild and from a rebuild with every input cut at that instant. The summary compares the yield with the price-ratio yield on the days both hold.

fields.name: date_utc
fields.unit: UTC ISO date, the decision day
fields.derivation: d

fields.name: rate_day
fields.derivation: d-1, the day whose close gives the rate

fields.name: state_block_timestamp
fields.derivation: block_timestamp of the state read for rate_day

fields.name: avax_per_savax
fields.derivation: avax_per_savax of c-chain-rpc.savax-state-daily on rate_day

fields.name: savax_supply
fields.derivation: savax_supply on rate_day

fields.name: savax_median_7d_pct
fields.derivation: median of savax_growth_30d_pct over days d-7 to d-1, when at least 4 have a value

fields.name: savax_days_7d
fields.derivation: days of the 7 with a yield

fields.name: price_ratio
fields.derivation: Allium's sAVAX price over its native AVAX price, else WAVAX, at the 24:00 UTC stamp of d-1

fields.name: market_discount_pct
fields.unit: percent; negative when sAVAX trades below its contract rate
fields.derivation: (price_ratio / avax_per_savax - 1) * 100

datasets.name: The label link to stake: P-Chain addresses paid by or paying an entity-labelled C-Chain address
studies: How Do Avalanche Validators Actually Think About Staking Rewards?
datasets.description: One row per P-Chain address, entity-labelled C-Chain address and direction: an export from the labelled C-Chain address that paid the P-Chain address, or an import by which the P-Chain address paid it. It is the one link from a C-Chain label to a stake: a validator's reward addresses or a delegation's funding address that appear here take the label's owner class. The class groups Allium's category into exchange, custodian, financial service, decentralised finance, MEV bot, wallet software and other; wallet software names the software an address uses, not its owner. The Foundation's mapping is joined beside the label and, for these addresses, is sourced from it. Counts, amounts and last times read only transactions before the held-back cut of 2025-11-19 00:00 UTC, and a link first seen on or after it is kept with held_back true and zero counts. The labels are one current snapshot with Allium's attribution time. Addresses stay in model tables: client outputs report linked stake as counts and shares by class, never an address, and nothing joins an address to any identity outside the chain. The summary gives the validator and delegated stake active at 2025-11-18 00:00 UTC by the class of the links seen before it. The check requires one row per address pair and direction, the same rows from a rebuild, and the same rows before the cut from a rebuild with the atomic transactions cut at the held-back instant.

fields.name: p_chain_address
fields.unit: P-Chain address, bech32 without the chain prefix
fields.derivation: an export's output owner address, or an import's P-Chain sender

fields.name: c_chain_address
fields.derivation: the export's sender or the import's recipient, labelled in allium.identity-labels-atomic

fields.name: link
fields.unit: export: the labelled address paid the P-Chain address; import: the P-Chain address paid it
fields.derivation: the atomic transaction's direction

fields.name: first_at
fields.derivation: the earliest block timestamp of the pair's transactions in that direction

fields.name: held_back
fields.unit: true when the link first appears on or after 2025-11-19 00:00 UTC
fields.derivation: first_at at or after the cut

fields.name: last_before_cut_at
fields.derivation: the latest block timestamp before the cut; empty for a held-back link

fields.name: transactions_before_cut
fields.derivation: atomic transactions of the pair and direction before the cut

fields.name: avax_before_cut
fields.derivation: their amount in nAVAX divided by 10^9
